title: Lantern Quay (synthetic example story)
note: Synthetic, public-domain example project for the story-editor test suite.

name: Narrator
mes:
[ 🕰️ Time 7:40 PM | 🗓️ Thursday, October 4, 1792 | 📍 Lantern Quay ]
The lamps along Lantern Quay come on one at a time, each lighter climbing his ladder with a taper and a cough. The tide is turning; the water slaps the pilings and smells of tar and cold weed. Ilse Calloway stands at the end of the quay with the harbour ledger under her arm, counting masts against the dark the way other people count rosary beads. Beside her, her younger sister Wren hugs a satchel of rolled charts to her chest.

"She's late," Ilse says. "The Gull's Due is never late."

name: Wren
mes: Wren shifts the satchel to her other arm and squints at the harbour mouth. "Late ships are the interesting ones," she says. "Nobody draws a chart of a ship that arrived on time."

name: Narrator
mes:
A shape breaks the line of the breakwater: a brig, low in the water, her topsails reefed though the wind is mild. She comes in without a pilot. When she warps alongside, the man who steps down first is broad and grey-bearded, with a coat too good for the weather and a smile too quick for the hour.

"Captain Varga," Ilse says, and opens the ledger. "Your manifest."

He hands it over with a flourish. "Salt fish, rope, and forty casks of Lisbon wine. Nothing that bites."

name: Wren
mes: Wren watches the crew carry the casks up the gangway. *Wine casks don't ride that low.* She says nothing, but she lets one of her chart rolls slip, and stoops to pick it up right beside the nearest cask, close enough to hear what's inside.

name: Narrator
mes:
The cask makes no sound of liquid. It makes the dry, papery whisper of something rolled tight and packed in straw. When Wren straightens, Varga is looking at her, still smiling, and the smile has stopped reaching his eyes.

"Mind the charts, girl," he says. "Paper is a fragile trade."

name: Narrator
mes:
[ 🕰️ Time 11:15 PM | 🗓️ Thursday, October 4, 1792 | 📍 The Harbour Office ]
The harbour office smells of lamp oil and damp wool. Ilse has the manifest open beside the ledger, and the clock on the wall has struck eleven twice in the time it has taken her to say nothing. Wren sits on the high stool by the window, where the lighthouse beam sweeps the glass every twelve seconds.

"The manifest says forty casks," Ilse says at last. "The weigh-house says forty casks. And the weigh-house says they weigh what wine weighs." She taps the page. "So why are you looking at me like that?"

name: Wren
mes: "Because I heard one," Wren says. "It wasn't wine, Ilse. It was paper. Rolled paper." She pulls the manifest toward her and holds it to the lamp. "And look at the seal."

name: Narrator
mes:
Under the lamp the wax seal shows a compass rose with a broken north point. Ilse goes very still. She knows that seal; every clerk on the coast knows it. It belongs to the Admiralty survey office at Kettering Point, and it is pressed only onto charts of the reef passages: the secret ways through the shoals that only naval pilots are meant to know.

"That isn't a manifest seal," Ilse says quietly. "That's a survey seal. Someone has cut it off a chart and pressed it here so the weigh-house wouldn't look twice."

name: Wren
mes: Wren slides off the stool. "Then the casks are full of survey charts. Stolen ones." She looks at the window, where the beam has just swept past. "Varga saw me listening. He'll move them before morning."

name: Narrator
mes: Ilse closes the ledger with both hands, as if it might fly open on its own. "If we wake the harbourmaster and we're wrong, I lose my post. If we're right and we wait, those charts are on a privateer by Sunday, and every reef passage on this coast is open to whoever's paying." She looks at her sister. "You're the one who heard it. You choose."

name: Narrator
mes:
[ 🕰️ Time 5:50 AM | 🗓️ Friday, October 5, 1792 | 📍 The Lighthouse Gallery ]
From the lighthouse gallery the whole harbour lies grey and small below, every mast a pencil stroke. The lamp behind Wren has just been dimmed for the morning; its brass is still warm. Down on the quay, a cart stands beside the Gull's Due, and men are rolling casks onto it in the half-dark, quickly, without lanterns.

The gallery door opens behind her. It is Captain Varga, a little out of breath from the stairs.

name: Wren
mes: Wren doesn't turn around. She keeps her eyes on the cart and her hand on the brass rail. "You came up a lot of stairs to look at a view, Captain."

name: Narrator
mes:
"I came up to make you an offer," Varga says. He stops a careful two paces away. "You draw charts. Good ones, I'd wager. There's a man in Brest who pays more for one honest chart of these waters than your sister earns in a year. Come down with me, forget what you heard, and you'll draw for him instead of for clerks."

Below, the cart's wheels creak. On the far side of the harbour, a single lamp is moving along the quay toward it: the harbourmaster's lantern, swinging the way it does when he walks fast. Ilse is carrying it.

name: Wren
mes: Wren finally turns. "My sister keeps the ledger," she says. "I keep the charts. Neither of us is for sale." Then she steps past him to the gallery bell and pulls the rope, hard, three times: the harbour's old signal for a ship in distress.

name: Narrator
mes:
The bell rolls out over the water. On the quay, the men at the cart freeze; lights come on in the customs house, then in the barracks along the mole. Varga looks at the girl at the bell rope for a long moment, and then, of all things, he laughs, a short, tired sound.

"Fragile trade," he says, and goes back down the stairs without hurrying, to meet whatever is waiting at the bottom.

Wren lets go of the rope. Her hands are shaking. Below her the whole harbour is waking up.
